questions.question: Explain why the trial balance splits into pre- and post-adjustment versions at year end, and which GAAP principles authorise the two Grade 10 adjustments.
questions.expected_answer: The pre-adjustment trial balance shows the ledger as the year's routine recording left it, but some year-end truths have no document — unused stationery, missing stock — so adjustments align the balances with fact, and the post-adjustment trial balance proves the equality survived them; final accounts are built only from the adjusted version. The consumable-stores adjustment is authorised by MATCHING (this year's statement carries only this year's consumption); the trading stock deficit by PRUDENCE (a discovered loss is recognised immediately, and the physical count is the fact the books adjust down to).

questions.question: Trace the year's profit through both final accounts at Thabo's Trading, naming the closing transfers and both profit figures.
questions.expected_answer: Sales R100 000 and Cost of Sales R80 000 close into the Trading account, whose credit balance of R20 000 is the gross profit — confirming the 25% mark-up on cost. The gross profit transfers to Profit and Loss, joined by Rent Income R6 000 (R26 000 assembled); the expenses close to the debit side — Salaries R12 000, Telephone R1 200, adjusted Stationery R800, Bank Charges R350, Trading Stock Deficit R150, total R14 500 — leaving a net profit of R11 500, which transfers to Capital because the profit belongs to the owner. The nominal accounts stand empty for the new year.

questions.question: Why is the year-end sequence a strict order, and what goes wrong if final accounts are prepared before the adjustments?
questions.expected_answer: Each step certifies the next: the pre-adjustment trial balance proves the routine books balance before anything is touched; the adjustments (full double entries in the GJ) bring balances to fact; the post-adjustment trial balance proves the equality survived; only then can final accounts compute profit and pass it to Capital, feeding the statements. Prepared early, the final accounts would carry every unadjusted rand — stationery overstated by R200 and stock overstated by R150 — so the profit would be wrong and the error would flow into the statements. The order is itself a control.
